entities.name: Central precocious puberty
observations: A 6-year-old boy with bilateral testicular volume around 5 mL, growth acceleration, and bone age advanced to 9 years has true gonadarche consistent with central precocious puberty.
In boys with central precocious puberty at this age, intracranial pathology must be excluded; idiopathic labeling requires brain MRI exclusion of a lesion.

entities.name: Benign premature adrenarche
observations: Usually causes body odor, acne, or pubic hair without pubertal testicular enlargement; the 5-mL testes and approximately 3-year bone-age advancement make it unlikely.

entities.name: 17-hydroxyprogesterone
observations: Morning 17-hydroxyprogesterone of 58 ng/dL is within the stated reference range and makes nonclassic 21-hydroxylase congenital adrenal hyperplasia unlikely.

entities.name: CNS-lesion-related precocious puberty
observations: A central puberty phenotype in a 6-year-old boy may be caused by an intracranial lesion; brain MRI is indicated before calling the condition idiopathic.
